references.text: The context explaining how Israel began to commit sexual immorality with the daughters of Moab and worship their gods, which led to attachment to Baal-Peor.
Moses' command to kill those who had attached themselves to Baal-Peor, as a consequence of the Lord's wrath.
A回顾 of the incident at Peor where Israel committed unfaithfulness against the Lord.
Moses reminds Israel that the Lord destroyed all who followed Baal-Peor.
The psalm describes how Israel attached themselves to Baal-Peer and ate sacrifices offered to dead gods, which aroused the Lord's wrath.
Hosea refers to Israel dedicating themselves to the shame of Baal-Peor and becoming as detestable as what they loved.
Joshua refers to the sin at Peor from which Israel had not yet cleansed themselves.
